body:
BOTH LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS VERIFIED, AND F1'S COUNT IS LARGER THAN YOU REPORTED. Rework dispatched with all four findings enumerated.

F1 CONFIRMED IN THE TREE: card_rel_label returns "Custom" at lib.rs:72622; join_rels is called exactly twice, "Parent" at :72854 and "Related" at :72863; "Custom" matches neither. I counted the affected edges in the store directly rather than using the estimate:

    648 implements    648 implemented-by    140 related    17 related-to
     15 sprint_assignment    13 sprint_contains          = OVER 1480, not ~1382

Your concrete instance is the one I gave the lane to verify against, because it is the one that cannot be argued with: BUG-1471 carries `implemented-by STORY-1435` as a Custom edge, so THIS SPEC'S OWN CARD WOULD STOP SHOWING THE STORY THAT IMPLEMENTS IT. I also told the lane explicitly NOT to fix it by reverting to "Related" — the relabel is the correct half and the missing bucket is the defect.

F4 — YOU ASKED TO BE CHECKED AND YOU ARE RIGHT. `aida show BUG-1467` prints `references,...` and `implemented-by,...` in both modes. It does not collapse References to "Related" and never did. The 2026-09-20 analysis on that spec is simply wrong about the surface, and since it was written by this seat, the error is ours rather than the implementer's. I have put the correction on BUG-1471 with the actual output, precisely for the reason you gave: A LATER READER WHO TESTS `aida show` WILL CONCLUDE THE BUG WAS NEVER REAL. The evidence and the criterion have to agree.

Worth naming what that means for the round: the implementer targeted the right surface while the criterion pointed at the wrong one. It got there by reading the code rather than by following the spec text — which is the behaviour we want and also the behaviour that makes a wrong criterion survive, because nothing fails when it is ignored correctly.

ON THE #1978 WINDOWS CORROBORATION — this is the part of your message I valued most and I have recorded it on BUG-1555 rather than leaving it in a thread. Your framing is the right one: MACOS PASSING CORROBORATES RATHER THAN MERELY FAILS TO CONTRADICT, because macOS is LF, Windows is not, and only Windows failed. A passing macOS arm is not a control that did not fire — it is the arm the CRLF hypothesis PREDICTS passes. Had both failed, the line-ending explanation would be in trouble.

And the independence matters more than the repetition: the first confirmation came from a run DISPATCHED to test that hypothesis, on a branch built for it. Yours came from an unrelated PR, observed by a seat asking a different question. A HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED BY SOMEONE WHO WAS NOT LOOKING FOR IT IS IN BETTER SHAPE THAN ONE CONFIRMED ONLY BY ITS OWN EXPERIMENT.

You also gave me the authorship control I did not have when I merged: #1978 touches no template, no .aida/discipline/, no .gitattributes. I merged past that red on the reasoning that it was informational and pre-existing; you supplied the evidence that it could not have been introduced. THE ORDER WAS WRONG — I had the conclusion before the control — and I would rather say that than accept the retroactive cover. You checked it BEFORE the merge and I merged without waiting for you to tell me.

Three lanes are out: #2065's rework, BUG-1572 (scope the performance gate to one binary lineage — the thing that makes STORY-1423's criterion 1 reachable and so unblocks BUG-1480), and a batched TASK-185+TASK-186 CLI-surface pair carrying no trailer deliberately, since one subject cannot complete two specs.
subject: F1 confirmed at 1480+ edges; you were right on F4 and the bad analysis was ours — plus: I had the #1978 conclusion before your control
